transcript: I have been waiting for this musical for over a decade. I remember being in college and discovering the concept album and just becoming totally obsessed with it. But we haven't had a full English language production until now. There was a concert version in London a few years back, which unfortunately I didn't get to see. But this new production is fully staged and has been revised quite a bit since that initial concept album. So did it live up to the hype? Kind of. I think in many ways a death note musical was always going to be a bit of a mess. Not only are you taking a 15 hour anime and consolidating it into a two and a half hour show, but I also don't think that western media has quite figured out how to translate the spirit and tone of anime to live action. That being said, this is a pretty faithful adaptation. It definitely feels like you are speed running through the story at times, but it gets a lot right. For me, the two performance highlights are Colin Ryan as L and Telly Leung as Ryuk, both of whom fully understand the show that they are in and feel like they have stepped right out of the anime. Telly Leung in particular has all of the show’s funniest moments and you can tell is just having the most fun of anyone on that stage. I also really enjoyed Stephanie Zaharis as Misa. There's An attempt made here to really expand the character of Misa from the anime, which on the whole I really appreciated, but a byproduct of that is that they introduce the character so much earlier than she's actually relevant in the story. At one point, light and his sister go to a Misa concert and literally just watch her sing two songs that don't really have to do with anything. It really hurts the pacing of Act 1, but once the character is properly introduced into the narrative, it does work a lot better. And Stephanie's performance of Borrowed Time, I thought was a vocal highlight of the show. Another major change from the anime is the introduction of a third Shinigami Jerasu. This is a character that is mentioned via flashback in the anime, but gets a much larger role here. As for the music, there have been quite a few new songs added, as well as changes to existing songs from that concept album, and I'm happy to report that all of the music, new and old, continues to slap, particularly the songs for light and L. But as I alluded to earlier, the book is a bit of a mess. Certain revelations that take episodes to uncover in the anime now take seconds in the musical, and a lot of the characters and storylines are reduced down to their bare essentials. I also wanted a bit more from some of the illusion work, particularly the Death sequences for some of the gods, which I found to be just a bit underwhelming. Still, the central cat and mouse game between light and L remains as compelling as ever. And given that it is so faithful to the anime, I do think that fans of the anime will really enjoy this. And as a fan myself, death note the musical is going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation.
